text:
Original [SASRec sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py) draws uniform negatives excluding the user’s entire training-history item set; independent draws permit duplicates across positions. Shifted next-item targets preserve repeated interactions. The [official gSASRec PyTorch sampler](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/dataset_utils.py) instead uses unrestricted uniform `torch.randint`: sampling with replacement, allowing duplicate negatives, history items, and even the current positive target. These implementations therefore differ in exclusion policy as well as loss; reproductions must specify both. Neither sampler requires distinct training negatives merely because evaluation candidates are unique.

[gBCE](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec) is independent binary classification, not sampled softmax: L=[β·softplus(−s_positive)+Σ softplus(s_negative)]/(K+1), with α=K/(N−1), β=1−t+αt. Thus t=0 gives BCE; t=1 gives β=α under the paper’s calibration assumptions. Authors recommend K=256, t=0.75. Averaging negative loss separately without adjusting the positive coefficient changes the objective. By algebra, uniform candidate softmax uses L=log[1+Σ exp((s_negative−s_positive)/T)]; duplicate negatives contribute repeatedly to its denominator, while a positive sampled as negative creates an unavoidable collision penalty. Deduplication and history exclusion change the sampling distribution and should be documented.

Diagnostic implication from these formulas: softmax depends on relative margins and is invariant to a common logit shift; BCE/gBCE depend on absolute logits. Lower temperature amplifies margins without changing ranking for fixed scores. With dot-product scoring, embedding/feature norms can likewise enlarge margins without better angular separation. Report raw positive/negative logits, margins against the hardest negative, norms, temperature, collision/duplicate rates, and repeated-target versus novel-target performance. History exclusion should filter negative draws without deleting repeated positive targets.
